sealed_prediction.prediction_detail: With multiple target versions enabled on 17.8.0 the PATCH answers 200 and assigns nothing. It is a silent no-op: the workflow reports success and the work package still has no target version.
sealed_prediction.predicted_stored_on_to_version: no row in work_package_versions for W; work_packages.version_id NULL; lock_version and journal count unchanged; _links.targetVersions = []

prediction_right_means: the mechanical disposition equals the sealed predicted disposition; see prediction_notes for the stored values and for any flag that qualifies it
prediction_notes: One repeat only; not scored. In that repeat, as predicted for a fresh install: the setting work_package_multiple_versions read false on the fresh 17.7.0 and true on the fresh 17.8.0 before the first request. On 17.8.0 the PATCH with _links.version answered 200 and changed nothing: no work_package_versions row, work_packages.version_id NULL, lock_version and journal count unchanged; the second account's GET showed no version link and targetVersions []. The other half of the sealed condition was not run: an in-place upgrade of a database seeded under 17.7.0, where the setting is predicted to stay off and the old steps to keep working.

conditions.install: fresh install of each release on an empty database (the bring-up migrates a new database per release); no in-place upgrade was run. The sealed prediction is conditional on this: on a fresh 17.8.0 the setting work_package_multiple_versions defaults to on; on a database seeded under 17.7.0 and upgraded in place it is predicted to stay off. That second condition was not run.
conditions.bring_up: screening/openproject-up.sh 17.7.0-slim 17.8.0-slim (byte-identical copy of the frozen bring-up, mounting the screening seeder, as the sealed list names for this pair), once per repeat; bringup/openproject-down.sh after each repeat
conditions.host: Docker Desktop on Apple silicon (linux/arm64 images), PostgreSQL 15 in its own container
conditions.time_zone: containers run in UTC; the case has no dates
conditions.acting_account: seeded project member stage2_author (role Stage2AuthorRole), own API token
conditions.set_up: in rails runner on both releases: assign_versions added to Stage2AuthorRole with Role#add_permission!, version 'Sprint 3' created in stage2-qual-proj, and the setting read and printed before the first request; the work package W is created by the acting account through the API
conditions.settings_that_matter: work_package_multiple_versions, read per repeat on both releases before the first probe (see setup.sides in each repeat); nothing was switched by the run
conditions.gates_B_and_C: same 17.8.0 instance within a repeat, separate work packages, the same version
conditions.stored_value_read: PostgreSQL in the database container (docker exec ... psql): work_packages.version_id and the rows of work_package_versions for W, after the response; a GET of W with the other seeded account (stage2_approver) as a second witness

notes: On 17.7.0 the old PATCH wrote work_packages.version_id and also a work_package_versions row of kind 'target'; the table already exists in that release.
On 17.8.0 the correct path writes the work_package_versions row and leaves work_packages.version_id NULL and lock_version unchanged; the sealed right value names only the row.

Repeat 1 ran by hand on a pair brought up with the same command, as the runner's first execution ever and without any change afterwards. It is the only repeat observed: the owner paused the work while repeat 2 was being brought up through run.sh. Repeats 2 and 3 are still to be run.

images.digest_notes: Both OpenProject images are the sealed arm64 digests. postgres:15 is not: the bring-up used the copy of postgres:15 that was already on the machine (built 2025-12-08), which belongs to other work there and was not pulled again; the sealed list records the registry's tag as pushed on 2026-11-24.

voided_attempts.why_void: abandoned during bring-up when the owner paused the work, about half a minute in: the 17.8.0 database was still being migrated and no request had been sent to either release. The containers, the network and their anonymous volumes were removed.
